title: North Carolina bicycle crash: 1 killed, 22 injured by impaired driver, officials say | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A group of cyclists was winding its way through a wooded, two-lane road outside of Raleigh on Saturday morning when a car crossed the center line and plowed into them, killing one and injuring nearly two dozen, authorities said.

A North Carolina man faces several felony charges after allegedly hitting the group and driving away. The local cycling club that organized the ride said the driver left “mass carnage in his wake.”

The cyclists were traveling together amid the fall colors along Optimist Farm Road, in Wake County, about 14 miles southwest of Raleigh, when an oncoming black passenger car crossed the center line and into the group, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol said.

The driver, later identified as 76-year-old Donald Robert Morris-Jones, continued driving before running off the left side of the roadway into a ditch, about a half-mile from where he hit the cyclists, authorities said.

Patrick Allen Turner, a 63-year-old cyclist from Cary, North Carolina, died in the crash, the highway patrol announced.

First responders found 22 others injured. Seven with more serious injuries were taken to regional trauma centers and 15 others were hospitalized, Chief LeRoy Smith of the Holly Springs Fire Department told CNN.

Morris-Jones, of Apex, North Carolina, was taken into custody and faces multiple charges, including hit-and-run causing serious injury or death, serious injury by a vehicle, and driving while impaired. He’s set to appear in court on Monday afternoon,court records show.

Although Morris-Jones does not appear to have a criminal record, he is considered an “overwhelming danger to society,” according to court records, and is under a $1 million bond.

CNN is working to determine whether he has legal representation.

Video of the aftermath of the crash showed law enforcement inspecting a stack of bikes propped up against a guardrail along the road. Some cyclists were still at the scene, video showed, including one man walking around with a phone to his ear, still wearing his bike helmet.

The group was on a morning ride organized each Saturday by the Capital Cycling Club, which has three groups biking at designated paces, the club’s board of directors told CNN in an emailed statement on Sunday evening. The accident resulted in severe injuries to multiple riders, the board said.

“We ask that drivers respect the right of cyclists to use the road,” the board statement said. “We are all in shock by the senseless decision by the individual that caused the collision.”

“We are working closely with law enforcement on their investigation. We will continue to follow this case closely as it proceeds to see that justice is done for our friends,” the statement continued.

One of the oldest cycling clubs in North Carolina, theCapital Cycling Clubhas “a rich history of charity work while participating in a variety of cycling races and events across Mid-Atlantic region,” according to its website. The club has been around for over 30 years, and its riders have years of experience with safety as a top priority, the board statement said.

Turner, the man who died in the crash, “was a strong, consistent, reliable and considerate rider,” the group said.

Shaun King from the nonprofit Bike Durham spoke to WRAL about the crash, calling it a “harrowing day for everyone in the cycling community.” He said he has ridden with the Capital Cycling Club before and has friends in the group, “so I’m nervously waiting to find out how connected I am to this particular experience.”

King said Turner and other cyclists will be remembered in a candlelight vigil on Bike Durham’s World Day of Remembrance, a day to remember pedestrians and cyclists killed in crashes, on November 15.

Another local cycling club, Team CBC, canceled their Sunday ride “Out of respect for the rider that was killed and all those who were injured,” offering their thoughts and prayers to those involved in the crash, according to aFacebook post.

Lin Osbourne told WRAL he is a member of the Capital Cycling Club and often rides with the cyclists that Morris-Jones is accused of striking, although he was not with them on Saturday.

“When things like this happen, it’s just a reminder that no matter how much we police ourselves, there are circumstances that are well beyond our control,” Osbourne said, adding that he has been road cycling for decades and intends to continue riding while taking precautions.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Nic F. Anderson and Jim Rogers contributed to this report.

CNN’s Nic F. Anderson and Jim Rogers contributed to this report.
